## QUESTION 1

1. __Describe the quality of your classification model using 2-3 different evaluation metrics.__ You also need to explain how to define/interpret each of the evaluation metrics you use.  

_My classification model is a Random Forest Classifier. It has a precision value of 77-82%. This metric is about how many times it can identify a house built before 1980. This model has a recall rate of 69-87%. This means that of the houses it chose, around 76% of them were actually built before 1980. F1-Score combines both precision and recall. This last metric shows that my model has around 76% accuracy._

```{python}
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

feature = df.select("netprice", "livearea", "stories")
target = df.select("before1980")

x_train, x_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(feature, target, test_size=0.1, random_state=20)

print(x_train.shape, y_train.shape)
print(x_test.shape, y_test.shape)

from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report
rf_classifier = RandomForestClassifier()
rf_classifier.fit(x_train, y_train)

rf_pred = rf_classifier.predict(x_test)

print(classification_report(y_test, rf_pred))

```


## QUESTION 2

1. __Justify your classification model by discussing the most important features selected by your model.__ This discussion should include a plot of permutation importance values for the most important features. Were there any features you thought would be importance but weren't?

_I thought that the number of stories a house has, its living area, and its net price would all be useful features to include. I assumed that other features such as having a finished basement or an attached garage would help, but they didn't raise my accuracy score at all. As I experimented with features, some of them actually brought my score down. So I settled on these three._

_AI use reflection_
**Link** to the original chat:

**The Impact**  How did using AI impact your learning?

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here

from sklearn.inspection import permutation_importance

result = permutation_importance(rf_classifier, x_test, y_test, n_repeats = 10, random_state = 42)

perms_imp = pl.DataFrame({'importance': result.importances_mean, 'vars': x_train.columns})

print(perms_imp.sort(['importance'], descending= True))
```
